A newborn male, delivered at 34 weeks gestation, is being assessed in the NICU for breathing
difficulties. The mother's pregnancy was notable for polyhydramnios, and the infant had Apgar scores
of 6 and 8 at 1 and 5 minutes. The mother is 33 years old, healthy, and this was her first pregnancy
with appropriate prenatal care. NICU staff observed excessive oral secretions and periodic oxygen
desaturation. Current vital signs show temperature 100.3°F (38.2°C), blood pressure 107/57 mmHg,
heart rate 130/min, and respiratory rate 30/min. Clinical examination reveals respiratory distress with
intercostal retractions and bilateral rales on lung auscultation. The abdomen appears moderately
distended. A chest X-ray shows coiling of the nasogastric tube within the esophagus. Which of the
following conditions should be investigated in this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Pyloric stenosis (B)
Esophageal atresia with tracheoesophageal fistula (C) Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (D) Laryngeal
web (E) Ventricular septal defect (F) Bronchogenic cyst (G) Hirschsprung disease (H) Choanal atresia

(I) Meconium ileus (J) Duodenal atresia
 A. Bronchogenic cyst
B. Duodenal atresia
C. Congenital diaphragmatic hernia
D. Hirschsprung disease
E. Choanal atresia
F. Laryngeal web
G. Ventricular septal defect
H. Pyloric stenosis
I. Meconium ileus
J. Esophageal atresia with tracheoesophageal fistula
